cohorts.summary: Beginners face a steep learning curve and sparse tutorials requiring outside resources.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is not beginner-friendly and lacks comprehensive explanations in the tutorial for core systems like occupations and traits.

citations.review_text: You think you're good at survival games? you're not. Project Zomboid taught me that and with every death, it will tech you something else. This is one of the most immersive zombie survival simulations out there. The only thing I do not like is how it is NOT beginner friendly at all, Even the tutorial kinda just throws you into it. Overall I would give this game an 8/10. Everything is well made and there are very few bugs I have encountered; I just wish it was more beginner friendly, because without youtube, I would've never figured some stuff out. I also wish the game explained some stuff better. Overall, great game, would totally recommend to any lover of survival games and challenges. If someone is reading this before they buy the game, don't get discouraged, keep at it, even if you have to step away from the game for a day or two, but don't just quit the game because you think you aren't good enough.

a very interesting game once you get use to the controls, the tutorial gives you good run down of the gameplay and what to expect, although the occupation and trait system takes some getting use to since it isn't explained in the tutorial and you have to balance them out in a way with specific builds, but you can easily join up on friends and experience first hand and explore while surviving the outbreak outside.

PZ is a very deep survival experience with seemingly endless crafting and character development.  It's unforgiving and a little intimidating at first, but the little things learned along the way make the next life more enjoyable.

i have had this game for about 18 hours and 17 of those hours were trying to fix my game and my mods without it crashing or my entire pc crashing. And 1 hour is me enjoying a game. Before my pc crashed again. Never got to play it since

citations.review_text:
Intrusting and different game. the complex sytems here and there get lost in their own and loose realism, but the impact witht he game is very good.

Thing to keep in mind:
this is NOT your usual 'hop in and ride shotgun' experience. there is a learning curve and it's steep. be ready for it. Not everybody's cup of tea, but if a gameplay video or two out there calls to you... this game is a 'one of a kind'

single_points.text: One reviewer says the menus take learning and repetition.

citation.review_text:
When I first picked up the game I could not get past the interface, the menus take learning and repetition but after getting used to them the game becomes very fun!

The game is still being updated at the time of this review; making excellent additions and performance updates. 13 years and counting!

Without a doubt Project Zomboid is one of the most difficult games I have ever played. It does not have to be though, mods and server config are both options! Project Zomboid is highly customizable letting players tune the game to be as easy as farming sim, or as difficult as spawning in a new game as a drunk with glass shards in your junk, in a house on fire.

10/10 would masochism again

claims.claim: Game updates routinely break existing save files and disable community mods.

citations.review_text: No respect for the modding community with the latest update. The absolute lack of foresight to add 42.21 as a branch for launching to be compatible with 42.21 mods while people wait for mods to update is appalling to me. Indie Stone, with full sincerity, do better.

After half a year, I decided to install a huge mod pack, tested it, and started playing.
A month later, update 42.22 comes out, with no way to roll it back.
After updating the mods, I came to the conclusion that my 150-hour save is completely broken — thanks to the devs for their hard work.

Useless update that broke all mods. Seriously? An update so that you can climb ladders and open doors with a crowbar - something that has been modded in ages ago. You have incredible mods coming out right now; A-Life, Viewpoint which gained so much traction for your game and yet, you decide to ruin savegames & mod configs for an update that took you 2 months to release? Again: Just for ladders & opening doors with crowbars. Get a grip. Either drop significant, larger updates or just stop and let the community handle the rest. We have already had enough problems with 42 unstable. Quit trying to jump on the band wagon you have not created.

I'm genuinely heartbroken  - due to the new update I've lost my 70 hours multiplayer character.  We've had it all, a big base, farm animals, nice vehicles and a ton of ammo.

I've tried fixing it with the help of my friends as well with the guides in the discussion tab. 
I'm unable to restore the game to the previous version incl. mdos and I have no desire to start all over again.

I'll stop playing, maybe someone will come up with a fix but for now I'm over it.

They are silencing people on the forums for complaining about broken saves once a update rolls up. I've played this game since pre-b41 days, and i've enjoyed it very much. I've played countless of hours in B41 with mods and without mods, and not once did a update brick my save. However, in b42, every single update bricks your saves. We were warned during unstable that that would occur, and yes it did. However, when the stable was announced, they mentioned saves wouldn't brick anymore. It would be smooth they said, updates would be meaningful they said. Stable does NOT feel stable. Every update since then makes the optimization worse, bricks saves, makes the game unplayable and they SILENCE everyone that complains. it's bad enough they let the white knights defend them, and even if the white knights are being toxic, they arent being silenced lmao. Get your act together.

I love the game. I hadn’t played for a while, but because of a new mod I started playing again. Devs, why not keep the previous stable version available on Steam? Steam has an option to select older versions of the game, so why not just leave the last stable build as a selectable option for people running mods? We don’t expect you to be technical support for mods, but at least give us that backup version until the modders can catch up with the new update. I’m only playing again because of a particular mod that’s now broken by this small update. And I’m pretty sure I didn’t have Steam set to automatic updates, but the game updated somehow anyway.

up until the most recent patch, id 100% recommend the game to anyone i spoke to. Most recent patch has broken hit detection for guns, so headshots dont count as damage for 85% of the hits you get. also broke SO MANY mods without the ability to rollback to previous version :(

Is Project Zomboid a fun game? Yes, for around two weeks every few months.

That's because after you've played vanilla for a little while, you'll realise there's a lot of QoL/performance issues, and a wide range of content available through mods. In fact, I'd go as far as to say that this game isn't playable without mods. Performance in the current build is much the same as it was in the previous build, despite performance improvements being one of the key aims of the patch.

The problem with modding the game is that after you've finished setting up your 200+ modlist, tweaking starting settings for your game (a process which can take days of restarting the game to see if things are just right for what you assume will be a lengthy playthrough), TIS will roll out an absolute nonsense patch that offers nothing of real substance, bricking your game. 

Now your mod list is out of date, and the previous build may or may not be available to download again through the beta list. Even if it is, certain mods need manually installing in the base game files, and they've now been overwritten. Every time a new update rolls out, you will have to edit the json file to allow the game to use more than 3gb of RAM.  This is a game that has made hundreds of millions on Steam, yet the studio can not hire people to rewrite the game and get us out of this java hellscape that we have existed in for 12 years.

At some point, someone is going to rewrite this game in a different engine with proper mod support, the game will run smoothly and I won't have to spend an entire weekend figuring out why my game is crashing because TIS decided to add climbing ladders to the game, something that has been possible through modding for 5 years. Until then, pirating the game and manually installing mods is a genuinely better player experience than buying it on Steam.
What's wrong with you s*ckers? Stop updating this god damn ten years old game! You are ruining our mods which are far better than your designs!

The devs recently shat out a new update. It fixed a bunch of bugs (that the community had already solved), allows players to open locked doors with a crowbar (there's a mod that does that, it works better than the official version), allows players to climb vertical stairs (there's a mod for that too, it's better too).
Do you know what they didn't fix in this bold new update? If a zombie goes near a bush, it turns invisible. A trash can is enough to hide an entire horde from view. A zombie upstairs can be waiting right in front of you, but because you're downstairs, it's invisible. You can't hit zombies you can't see, but they sure as fuck can get you. 
Most deaths are because of bullshit line of sight problems and poor design decisions. So, the devs shat out a new version. It added nothing worthwhile, but it broke the mods, which are what actually make this game enjoyable.
tl;dr: don't give these people your money.

This game has been in development for over a decade. The devs steal ideas from mods, then add them to the game and break your saves. Not for a significant improvement, but for ladders. Yeah, last update added the ability to climb ladders. HOORAY! If you buy it, you must accept that the game is incomplete, and judging by the pace of development, MAYBE your grandkids will get version 1.0. More likely your great grandchildren.
add a 42.21 rollback option, mods are broken and the game won't launch

TL/DR Grab the game on sale, disable automatic updates (to stop IS from breaking your mods), backup frequently and mod the hell out of it. It will be fun. Of my 6-700 hours almost every moment has been modded except the first 2-3. The base game is just that, the base game. Its an alright foundation to be built on by mods because once you understand the core gameplay loop, you realize it lacks any real motivating reasons to keep playing and becomes stale quickly. Mods remedy this entirely. If you are choosing to purchase this you should understand the bad development and communication practices of Indie stone by reading the rest.

Project Zomboid at its core is a great concept that indie stone has failed to iterate on or expand meaningfully in 10 years. In my opinion It exists in the state it is now to keep the development team in cashflow by selling new players a game that is still "in active development" (more on this later) - while allowing them to maintain minimum effort and excuse lazy development. Their team lacks effective leadership and it shows. 

The game stands out and maintains relevance due to the incredible modding community around the game, despite Indie Stones best efforts to *uck things up with every "update" they push. The modding community consistently implement 100s of new ways to play, interact and often fix things IS has not yet fixed, or have broken themselves. And mods customize the world of zomboid including implementing features that this dev team has ignored or been incapable of implementing for YEARS. NPCs, ladders, water that is ACTUALLY water and not a tile with a few blue pixels. The list goes on.

13 years of early access on steam (and they were on Desura before that), with multiple "directional shifts" that have essentially reset or majorly set back development progress, the latest being b42 so they could redesign how crafting and water work (something no one was asking for). This build was conveniently pushed out the door at the same…

I hate that I love this game. There are so many things done wrong and so little few things done right that you have to play the game with multiple mods to add more meat on the bones of this game. Then, there's a patch which ruins this whole process and also, breaks the game (even vibe coding wouldn't be this bad).

Great game, but man there are so many flaws. Got excited to play again for the first time in a few months after the update, especially seeing the reworked towns and new mechanics in build 42. I've been having a great time while playing, but the issue is being able to continue my saves. There is no reason I should have to restart a save after every update. I've tried backing up the saves and it doesn't work. This issue needs resolve before this game can ever be a finished product

claims.claim: Multiplayer setup and playing with mods involves significant bugs, desync, and troubleshooting difficulties.

citations.review_text:
I've been playing Project Zomboid for a while, and honestly, I'm getting tired of making excuses for this game.

First of all, the game engine is outdated as hell. This game has been in development since 2013, and somehow it still feels like the developers haven't made any meaningful progress when it comes to the actual technology behind it. We're talking about a game that's been around for over a decade, yet basic things still feel unnecessarily clunky, outdated and poorly optimized.

And here's what really gets me: a handful of modders have managed to create their own first-person experience using their own solutions (Viewpoint, for example), while the actual developers are still struggling to bring this kind of functionality to the game properly. How is it that independent modders are pushing the boundaries of what's possible, while the people developing the actual game seem so reluctant to move forward? How much money does this game need to make before the developers finally decide to invest in improving their own technology?

Then there's multiplayer with mods. Holy shit. Trying to play this game with friends while using mods is an absolute nightmare. Random bugs, compatibility issues, completely unexplained problems and troubleshooting that feels like a full-time job. Something breaks, you spend hours trying to figure out what went wrong and there's barely any reliable documentation or proper troubleshooting guides available. I've asked for help on Discord multiple times, tried looking for solutions and still ended up getting nowhere. You're basically left to figure everything out yourself.

What makes it even worse is that some of these issues are incredibly difficult to fix because there simply aren't enough proper guides explaining what's causing them or how to solve them. You shouldn't have to become a damn programmer just to enjoy a modded multiplayer session with your friends.

And let's not forget the in-game optimization. It's genuinely terrible. For a…

Yikes look at those hours. I've been patient with this game for a long time.

This game has been in development for so long that the platforms it was originally designed for are no longer common used. Updates are routinely unstable. Basic features are slow dripped. Poor UI and QoL decisions. Multiplayer desync problems. You will spend as much time fighting against the game simply breaking as you will actually trying to play it.

I literally have no clue what the fuck is happening to this game. This game used to work just fine, I was able to set up servers and play with friends no problem, and now I simply cannot do anything, can't even launch the game. No mods, fresh install, I even JUST reinstalled all of windows. Nothing, doesn't budge. Troubleshooted for hours. And when it WAS able to launch, creating a server for me and my friends was a fucking nightmare, and ended up not even working at all, no mods, no extra bullshit, this game is not stable at all.

I cannot at all reccomend you buy this as of now, especially if you want a game you can just jump into, cause, it WILL break, even if you don't encounter the bugs I do, you WILL encounter bugs, that WILL make the game unenjoyable, or unplayable.
